title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Reed spaces documented for studying, making, meeting, performing, and student-led activity.

cards.title: Student Center
cards.subtitle: Lounge, study, and meeting space
cards.notes: Bring your work or a small group, then use the reservable rooms when available; card-swipe access is required.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub with space for independent work and group meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Student Center is open to students for lounging, studying, and meeting, with spaces reservable for individual or group use.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces — Office for Student Engagement
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 8:30 AM–midnight daily; card swipe is required.

cards.title: Student Union
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center gathering space
cards.notes: Use the shared building for a late study session or a planned event, and enter through the northwest doors with your swipe access.
cards.short_summary: A centrally located student space adjacent to the Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed identifies the Student Union as a student space and says it is open 24 hours during the academic year when classes are in session.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces — Office for Student Engagement
cards.access_notes: During the academic year, it is open 24 hours except college breaks; northwest-door swipe access is required.

cards.title: Publications Office
cards.subtitle: GCC 047 student-publication workspace
cards.notes: If you contribute to a student publication, coordinate with its editors before using this GCC workspace for reporting, layout, or production.
cards.short_summary: A designated workroom for Reed’s student publications.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed lists the Publications Office in GCC 047 as working space for the college’s various student publications.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces — Office for Student Engagement
cards.access_notes: Check student-space access guidelines and publication-specific arrangements before entering.

cards.title: Pool Hall
cards.subtitle: Student-run games and music space
cards.notes: Drop in to play pool, listen to the jukebox, or spend time with the writing on the walls; ask the manager about access details.
cards.short_summary: A six-table student space built around pool, music, and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes the Pool Hall as an all-access space with six pool tables, a jukebox, and a furnished office.
cards.access_notes: The college calls it an all-access space; confirm current access with the Pool Hall manager.

cards.title: Print Shoppe
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center screen-printing space
cards.notes: Plan a shirt or poster project and check in with the student-run shop before using its screen-printing equipment; bring your own blank garment.
cards.short_summary: A student-run place to make screen-printed projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Print Shoppe is a student-run silk-screening space in Gray Campus Center with equipment for printing T-shirts.
cards.access_notes: Coordinate use and equipment access with the student-run Print Shoppe.

cards.title: Reed Bike Co-op
cards.subtitle: Guided bicycle-repair workshop
cards.notes: Bring your bike for guided repair, learn a maintenance task, and use the available tools with help from the co-op’s mechanics.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on workshop for repairing bikes and learning mechanical skills.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says its Bike Co-op guides people through their own repairs and helps students become mechanics who can assist others.
cards.access_notes: Ask the co-op about current workshop access and availability of replacement items.

cards.title: Student Darkroom
cards.subtitle: Black-and-white photo developing space
cards.notes: Sign up for a training or refresher, then develop and print black-and-white photographs using the student darkroom’s shared materials.
cards.short_summary: A student space for learning and practicing analog black-and-white photography.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Student Darkroom provides free loaner cameras, film, chemicals, paper, and training for black-and-white photography.
cards.access_notes: Free trainings are offered; seek a refresher if you need help using the space.

cards.title: Performing Arts Building
cards.subtitle: Atrium, rooftop patio, and performance rooms
cards.notes: Look for a public performance or campus event, then pause in the atrium or rooftop patio; respect rooms reserved for classes and productions.
cards.short_summary: A shared arts building with flexible theatres, rehearsal rooms, and gathering areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Performing Arts Building has common spaces for collaborative work, a rooftop garden, exhibition spaces, and an atrium.
cards.access_notes: Performance and classroom spaces may be scheduled; use public or permitted areas only.

cards.title: Eliot Hall Chapel
cards.subtitle: Friday at Four concert setting
cards.notes: Check the music calendar for a Friday at Four program, then attend the performance in the chapel when the event is open to the community.
cards.short_summary: A historic chapel used for recurring student, staff, and guest performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s music department says the Chapel in historic Eliot Hall is used for Friday at Four concerts featuring staff, students, and guest performers.
cards.access_notes: Attend during a listed program or other authorized event; verify the current calendar before going.

cards.title: Vollum College Center
cards.subtitle: Map-listed lecture hall and lounge
cards.notes: Use the lounge for a change of study setting, and check campus listings before attending any lecture scheduled in the building.
cards.short_summary: A campus building with both lounge and lecture-hall functions.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s current campus map identifies Vollum College Center as containing a lecture hall and lounge.
cards.access_notes: Access can vary with classes, lectures, and campus operations.
